patch.value: Resource admission drops installed extension type/field registries from validation and revision lookup

Tracks gh:unbraind/pm-csv#214 (filed 2026-10-29, missed by the blind issue watch). admission.ts on current main still calls resolveItemTypeRegistry(settings) without the active workspace extension registrations in both scan() and the revision-lookup path (locateItem type_to_folder), so an installed extension-defined item type becomes a row_invalid admission rejection and revision reads use a narrower schema than the writer. Verified on main 2026-11-02: the one-argument resolver call remains. The bounded-admission feature that delivered PR #213 is closed, so this regression needs its own fix: activate the target workspace extensions (or pass the resolved registry) before scan and revision lookup, and add an admission regression with an extension-defined type and field.

## Classification and tested revision
Static integration finding in PR #213 at `10678a7187146cd09077a48ffed7003535dda16d`, supported by a bounded public-SDK resolver control on `@unbrained/pm-cli 2026.10.28` / Node24.22.1. This is not a claim that the whole native import workflow was independently reproduced.

## Evidence
[admission.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-csv/blob/10678a7187146cd09077a48ffed7003535dda16d/admission.ts):
- `scan` calls `resolveItemTypeRegistry(settings)` without the active extension registrations, then treats a row type missing from that registry's `alias_to_type` as invalid.
- `admissionTargetRevision` likewise uses that incomplete `type_to_folder` for `locateItem`, and reads the document without registered extension field names.
- `admitCSV` wraps settings consistency, but does not itself activate the requested workspace's extensions.

The public SDK resolver's second argument defaults to null; it does not implicitly incorporate the active registry. A synthetic control for20 distinct extension-defined types passed80 assertions: `resolveItemTypeRegistry({}, {item_types:[{types:[{name:"FixtureBridge",folder:"fixture-bridges"}]}]})` includes the type and folder, while the exact one-argument call used here omits both. No real tracker, credentials or provider was used.

## Expected / impact
An installed extension-defined type supported by the native SDK should not become a `row_invalid` admission rejection merely because the resource-admission path drops the target workspace registry. Revision lookup must resolve the same types/folders and preserve all registered fields as the actual mutation path. Otherwise legitimate imports into extensible workspaces are refused, and target/history checks can operate with a narrower schema than the writer.

This follows the feature's verified [canonical record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-csv/blob/10678a7187146cd09077a48ffed7003535dda16d/.agents/pm/features/pm-csv-bounded-admission.toon): reuse SDK schema/status/transaction capabilities rather than adding a dialect/journal. It also preserves the existing public-SDK extensibility contract. Settings-defined custom types are not the same test as installed extension types.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
1. Activate the explicitly selected target workspace through the public SDK and pass its active registrations to type resolution; use the complete registered field set for authoritative document/history reads.
2. A plain synthetic tracker with a real installed schema extension, a custom type/folder, and opaque string/object fields passes full admission and bounded admitted import without losing fields or history.
3. Cover default and injected/direct SDK entry points, JSON/TOON tracker formats, and strict unknown-field policy. Wrong workspace registrations must not bleed between calls.
4. Invalid/unregistered types still refuse; late-invalid-row zero-write behavior, resource bounds and source/settings/revision fences remain unchanged.
5. No copied per-package registry or business semantics; reuse public core primitives.

## Limits
The resolver omission and its direct branch consequences are static evidence; full native admission/apply reproduction, concurrency and recovery remain untested here. No claim of an observed field-loss incident. Existing all-status issues/PRs and the canonical feature were checked before filing.
Admission omits installed extension type/field registries from validation and revision lookup
